stem:
A 4-year-old is brought to the ED because his mother found him sleepy and very unsteady on waking this morning. He had spent the night before at his father’s house. He is difficult to rouse but can answer basic questions. He has slurred speech, multidirectional nystagmus, truncal/gait ataxia, and marked shakiness when trying to handle objects. Tone, power, and reflexes are normal. He says he had some “orange lollies” from his dad’s cupboard last night. His mother recalls the father takes a daily medication for “funny turns”. Blood tests and MRI are normal. A urine toxicology screen is pending.

What is the most likely explanation for the child’s presentation?
explanation: The presentation is most consistent with acute drug intoxication, likely ingestion of a parent’s medication, causing sedation, ataxia, nystagmus, and slurred speech with otherwise normal examination and imaging.
rationale: The key clues are sudden onset after overnight stay with access to unknown medication, drowsiness, ataxia, nystagmus, dysarthria, and normal MRI/labs. This pattern is most consistent with drug intoxication.

optionExplanations.A: Usually follows a recent viral illness and causes gait ataxia without prominent sedation or drug-like toxidrome features.
optionExplanations.B: A chronic, progressive condition with telangiectasia and immunodeficiency, not an acute isolated episode.
optionExplanations.C: Acute onset after access to a parent’s medication plus drowsiness, nystagmus, slurred speech, and ataxia strongly suggests intoxication.
optionExplanations.D: Would more likely cause progressive symptoms and raised intracranial pressure or focal neurological signs; MRI is normal.

Instructions

Question 1 & 2 relate to this case

Case 1

A 4 year old is brought into ED as his mother found him to be sleepy and very unsteady on waking up this morning. His parents have been separated for 2 years and he had spent the night before at his father’s house. The boy has not been otherwise unwell and there is no concern about trauma. He is developmentally normal and his growth has been following the 75th centile lines.

On examination weight, head circumference and height are on 75th centiles. His BP is 100/70 and he is afebrile. He does not have a rash. He is difficult to rouse but can answer basic questions. His speech is slurred but you are able to make out that he had some ‘orange lollies’ last night that he found in his dads cupboard. He cannot walk or sit without falling to both sides. He has nystagmus in all directions and slurred speech but the rest of his cranial nerves are normal. He has normal tone, power and reflexes. He is very shaky when trying to get the lid off your pen and cannot replace the lid. He wants to fall asleep. You question his mum about any possible medications that he could have had access to and she has a vague recollection that his father has ‘funny turns’ for which he takes a daily medication but she can’t recall what it’s called.

You do screening blood tests including a full blood count, liver function tests and a blood gas and they are normal. You request an MRI and it too is normal. A urine toxicology screen is still pending.
